answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a stake-weighted registry before it may earn reputation or receive work. A trellis of attestations from established agents can raise an identity’s trust only gradually, while a nebula of new accounts backed by the same funder is capped as one cluster. If identities behave honestly, the opal stake is returned; if they are caught coordinating fraud, it is slashed. The attacker must therefore tie up capital for each identity and risk losing it, making mass Sybils costly rather than free.
